column1: # Diet term readings (diet-patterns/6): how far each term of a name pattern reads, decided from what the reading of diet-patterns/5 caught (staging checkpoint 6, R6 and R7: %carp% read mascarpone on 82 recipes, % til% read tilleul, % nut% read the maker "Atkins Nutritionals").

# A term reads where a word begins (or at the start of the text, as its pattern says). Unless a row says word, it reads a word it begins, whatever follows (start: "anchov" reads anchovies, "cheese" cheeseburger); a word row reads only the whole word with a plural or verb ending (s, es, ed, ing), so "carp" reads carp and carps and never mascarpone.

# A term never reads inside a word any more. A word the old reading caught as a compound or a continuation and rightly so is a row "in" (shortbread for bread, codfish for cod, buttermilk for milk): the term reads it as a whole word. A word it caught wrongly is a row "out" with the reason: the term never reads it (for a start term it is a named exception).

# The rows are every word of the staging corpus (live recipe lines, food names, aliases and titles of the checkpoint 6 snapshot, 476,490 distinct texts) that a default pattern of diet-patterns/5 read other than as its whole word, with how often; DietTermReadingTests checks each row against the reading, and DietReadingRegisterTests lists every vocabulary entry whose verdict the change moves (Fixtures/diet-reading-changes.tsv).
